title: Welcome to Agents Week
description: Agents Week explores how cloud infrastructure must evolve to serve autonomous agents rather than human browsers. Join us as we unpack the storage, execution, and security primitives needed for an agent-native web.

title: A DNS Investigation of LenAI’s ErrTraffic ClickFix Distribution Network
description: An analysis of LenAI's ErrTraffic ClickFix infrastructure uncovered new DNS links, exposing malicious domains, IPs, typosquatting clusters, and email connections that broaden threat visibility and support stronger detection and incident response through expanded network intellige…

title: Why Nordic Domain Days Has Become a Defining Event for the Domain Industry
description: Nordic Domain Days drew 450 attendees from 77 countries, underscoring its growing international reach. Blending practical insights with close-knit networking, the event continues to strengthen the global domain community and its collaborative spirit.

title: An API for MoQ: provision your own isolated relays
description: Last year we made every Cloudflare server a Media over QUIC (MoQ) relay. Now the new provisioning API lets you create your own isolated relay and control who can publish and who can only watch.

title: The AI Enclosure Movement
description: The battle over open-source AI echoes England's Enclosure Movement, pitting collaboration against proprietary control as technology firms compete to shape innovation, economic power and the future governance of the digital commons.

title: Dogfooding at scale: migrating cdnjs to Cloudflare’s Developer Platform
description: We moved cdnjs, serving 9 billion requests a day, entirely onto Cloudflare's Developer Platform. That means we’re running one of the Internet's busiest open-source CDNs on our own building blocks, and we pushed Workflows and Workers limits higher for everyone.

title: Two Providers, a Stubborn Plateau and a Very Long Tail: Email in the Tranco Top-1M
description: Ten years of DNS measurements reveal three trends across the Internet's most popular domains: email continues to consolidate around two providers, DMARC enforcement has hit a plateau, and a surprisingly large long tail of infrastructure defies easy classification.

title: Secretariat restructuring and staffing update
description: There have been a few changes in IETF Administration LLC staffing since January of this year (2026) including the recent insourcing of the Secretariat, which are summarised here to give an overall view of the staffing structure.

title: BGP topics from IETF 126
description: BGP ORIGIN, ASPAs, PAVA, and ASRAs at IETF 126.

title: Call for Participation: DNSSEC and Security Workshop at ICANN87 (21 October 2026)
description: ICANN is inviting proposals for its DNSSEC and Security Workshop at ICANN 87, offering experts and practitioners a platform to share insights on DNS security, routing security, browser security, and emerging Internet infrastructure challenges.

title: Premium Domain Demand Reaches New High in Radix’s H1 2026 Report
description: Radix's H1 2026 Premiums Report reveals record premium domain registrations, rising renewals, and growing demand for short, brand-defining names, underscoring how businesses increasingly view premium domains as strategic assets for long-term growth and digital identity.

title: From Human Trust to Machine Cryptography: The Infrastructure Deficit in AI Interoperability
description: As AI agents begin collaborating across the open internet, the absence of trusted identity, authorization, and accountability frameworks threatens interoperability, making cryptographic trust infrastructure essential to building a secure and scalable agentic economy.

title: Asia’s Invisible Tariff: Why AI Capital Is Underweighting the Markets That Want It Most
description: As trillions flow into AI infrastructure, Asia's biggest emerging markets remain underfunded. Beyond power and geopolitics, obscure internet governance, IPv4 allocation, and regulatory ambiguity may be quietly shaping where hyperscale capital chooses to build.

title: ICANN Wiki, SHE.africa, AI, and the Integrity of Digital Platforms
description: As AI increasingly relies on digital archives, the quiet revision of ICANNWiki entries raises broader questions about platform accountability, historical integrity, and whether institutions can reshape the records that future researchers and machines will treat as fact.

title: Post-quantum authentication to origins is now supported
description: Cloudflare now supports post-quantum (PQ) authentication when connecting to customer origin servers via Authenticated Origin Pulls and Custom Origin Trust Store. This is the first step towards providing PQ authentication for all Cloudflare products.

title: DNS topics at IETF 126
description: Recursive resolver DNS query behaviour, Post-quantum DNSSEC, Optimistic DNS, Automating DNS delegation management, and more from IETF 126.

title: Microsoft Launches AI Cybersecurity Model to Boost MDASH Performance and Cut Costs
description: Microsoft has unveiled a specialist cybersecurity AI model powering MDASH, claiming higher benchmark performance and lower costs while launching Project Perception, an agentic security platform designed to help defenders counter increasingly automated cyber threats.

title: Amazon Targets Satellite-to-Phone Market With 5,105-Satellite Leo Expansion
description: Amazon has outlined plans for a 5,105-satellite constellation that will connect smartphones directly from space, expanding emergency and mobile services while intensifying competition in the fast-growing satellite-to-device communications market.

title: Natural disasters and government interference: examining Q2 2026’s major Internet disruption events
description: Cloudflare Radar tracked Internet disruptions driven by natural disasters, government-mandated shutdowns, and DNSSEC key rollovers over the last quarter. This post analyzes traffic telemetry to explain how these events impacted global connectivity.

title: ASO AC delivers Recommended Draft RIR Governance Document to NRO EC
description: The ASO AC has delivered the ASO AC Recommended Draft RIR Governance Document to the NRO EC for its consideration.

title: Hooray for the sockets interface
description: In 1983, BSD 4.2 introduced sockets, treating network communication like file I/O. This simplification sped UNIX adoption of shared protocols and services, marking a key turning point in modern networking.

title: We’re open-sourcing our privacy proxy CLI
description: pvcli is a curl-like tool designed to simplify the testing of complex privacy protocols like OHTTP.

title: Secure by default: How ‘HSTS-Enforced’ could finally close the web’s oldest backdoor
description: Guest Post: The current web still relies on a legacy assumption that website should be accessible over unencrypted HTTP unless it explicitly signals otherwise. HSTS-Enforced builds on top of HSTS by inverting its security model.

title: BGP ORIGIN attribute manipulation and its impact on the Internet
description: By doing in-depth testing, we found nearly 70% of BGP paths experience ORIGIN attribute rewrites by transit providers seeking traffic advantages. We examine the global impact of this practice and argue for deprecating ORIGIN in route selection.

title: The delicate art of cryptographic maintenance: When small certs break big chains
description: Around mid-2026, we began receiving user complaints about certificate validation failures. The failure wasn’t a single bug, but the collision of optimization and slow distribution.

title: Introducing Cache Response Rules
description: Perhaps you’ve seen something that should sail out of cache get dragged back to the origin by a stray Set-Cookie or Cache-Control, headers that can be difficult to change on the origin itself. Cache Response Rules is the fix, applied at the right time.

title: What's ARP Got to Do with It?
description: It's only ARP. It works. So how much can it really matter? The answer lies beyond ARP itself, in the IPv4 layer cake that grew around it over four decades. The IPv4 internet is not going away in bounded time, and nobody should pretend otherwise.

title: [Podcast] DNS query duplication
description: Why does APNIC Labs experimental systems see almost all DNS queries twice or more?

title: Inside a Shutdown: BGP Evidence from an Operator Who Was There
description: When Bangladesh vanished from the global routing table in July 2024, public routing data captured the event as it unfolded. Drawing on first-hand observations from inside one affected network, this article explores what that data can and cannot tell us.

title: Bringing APNIC closer to Members: SANOG to host next APNIC Sub-Regional Forum
description: APNIC’s next Sub-Regional Forum at SANOG in Kathmandu, Nepal, will bring Internet operations, policy, and community discussions closer to Members in South Asia.

title: Don’t Get Your Wires Crossed: Appropriate Use Cases for IPv6-Only vs. IPv6-Mostly
description: Terms like IPv6-only and IPv6-mostly are a clear example of how IETF terminology often lacks clarity. IPv6 expert Jordi Palet Martínez, explains why the correct use of these terms requires specifying a scope of application.

title: How the 2026 World Cup affected Internet traffic
description: We analyzed global HTTP traffic to explore how kickoff times, streaming habits, and hydration breaks reshaped online activity worldwide. From late-night traffic surges to halftime browsing spikes, here is how the world connected during the global tournament.

title: Beyond Origin Validation: Four Classes of Routing Attack Nobody Is Validating
description: RPKI has made real progress against prefix hijacking. But when you map every known class of BGP attack against the defences that exist, four of them turn out to sit entirely outside cryptographic validation: handled with local filters, static thresholds and reactive response.

title: APNIC 62 workshops build practical skills for modern network operations
description: APNIC 62 features three hands-on workshops that help network professionals automate operations, strengthen security, and deploy next-generation routing technologies.

title: Cloudflare Internal DNS is now generally available
description: Cloudflare Internal DNS brings authoritative and recursive DNS for private networks to the same global network and control plane that runs Cloudflare's Zero Trust, networking, and public DNS.

title: Who's Running All Those Tiny RPKI Servers?
description: Who runs the hidden infrastructure behind secure Internet routing? An internship report from SIDN Labs looks beyond the RIRs at the independently operated RPKI publication servers helping to secure BGP.

title: IPv6 address planning: From ‘bit conservation’ to ‘elegant alignment’

description: Digital sovereignty is not simply good or bad. The commons test offers a practical framework for assessing whether different strategies expand choice, preserve interoperability, strengthen resilience and support meaningful participation, or create new dependencies and chokepoints…

description: The IETF Community Survey provides a comprehensive assessment of community demographics, engagement patterns, and perceptions of organizational effectiveness. Read the full findings below.

title: A Farewell to ARPs: IPv4 Service on IPv6-Only Networks
description: IPv6-only networks often still depend on IPv4 subnets and ARP. This article introduces an IETF proposal to eliminate both, allowing IPv4 to operate as a service over IPv6-only infrastructure without translation or tunnelling.

description: The RIPE Chair Team rounds up the latest developments across the community, from RIPE 93 preparations and policy work to governance updates and community activities.

description: Sometime before 19 June, we hope you’ll set aside some time to share your feedback with us as we conduct our 2026 Customer Satisfaction Survey to gain a better understanding of our performance in all areas of the organization.
